analyst_view.overall: Early view: Two sides heading the wrong way: Augsburg are winless in seven league games under Manuel Baum despite scoring in every match, and Mainz lost four of their last five in all competitions before the break. Mainz have taken nine of their ten points away from home, though, which makes this trip more promising for Urs Fischer's side than the table suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Augsburg's league games have produced 40 goals in nine (joint-most in the league) and Mainz's 37, with Mainz scoring most of theirs away through Phillip Tietz, Sheraldo Becker and Benedict Hollerbach. Both defences concede freely, Mainz nine in three games in late October.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners. Augsburg's wing-backs give them width at home and Mainz's pace-based counters do not produce many corners, but nothing in the recent games points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean slightly higher: Fischer has talked about a 'slightly nasty' style, Stefan Posch was sent off at Elversberg, and a meeting of two sides under pressure tends to be scrappy. Augsburg have been fairly clean lately (no bookings against Freiburg), which stops me going much higher.

shots.text: The site has 31.7 shots. Mainz away rely on quick transitions rather than long spells of pressure, so their 13.8 looks high, and Augsburg's 17.9 is generous for a side that has been outplayed in several recent games. I lean a little lower on volume, while still expecting goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 on target. That fits my higher goals view: Augsburg's Michael Gregoritsch and Kade have both scored recently and Mainz's Tietz leads their line, while both defences let opponents get shots away. I stay level.
